v: As some were talking about the temple and how it was decorated with beautiful stones and gifts, he said,
“As for these things which you see, the days will come, in which there will not be left here one stone on another that will not be thrown down.”
b: In this passage, as people marvel at the temple's splendid decorations, Jesus prophesies that it will be destroyed, with not one stone left on another. The prophecy points to the destruction of the Jerusalem temple, and it also symbolizes God's judgment on a people who relied on outward form while neglecting inner life. The temple was magnificent, but if the people's hearts are not faithful to God, it ultimately loses its meaning and is brought down.

Jesus' prophecy reminds us that outward beauty and glory do not last; what truly matters is the relationship of our hearts with God. Our lives should not merely chase worldly success and honor, but seek integrity and godliness before Him. Everything in this world will pass away, but our relationship with God is eternal.

Through this passage God tells us to fix our eyes on eternal values rather than temporary things. Let us reflect on whether there are times we have leaned too heavily on outward form or material things, and adjust our priorities so that God is first in our lives.
q: In your life, do you focus too much on outward achievement and honor? How can you give more attention to your eternal relationship with God?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for reminding us to focus on eternal values rather than passing glory. Help us put our relationship with You first, and keep our hearts from being drawn away from You by the temptations of the world. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: They asked him, “Teacher, so when will these things be? What is the sign that these things are about to happen?”
He said, “Watch out that you don’t get led astray, for many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and, ‘The time is at hand.’ Therefore don’t follow them.
When you hear of wars and disturbances, don’t be terrified, for these things must happen first, but the end won’t come immediately.”
b: In this passage the disciples ask Jesus about the signs of the end. Jesus first warns them to be careful not to be deceived, especially by those who come claiming to be the Christ. He adds that even when they hear of wars and uprisings they should not be terrified, for these things must happen first, but the end will not come at once. His words call us to spiritual alertness and discernment, so that we are not swept along by every end-times panic.

Jesus' warning reminds us that our life of faith should not be shaken by outside fears or the claims of false prophets. We should focus on Jesus' teaching and God's word, and keep peace and confidence in our hearts. Even when the world is in turmoil, as Christians we know that God is in control, and our lives and our future are in His hands.

Through this passage God reminds us that, however circumstances change, our faith should stand firm on Jesus Christ. He is our refuge; in Him we find peace and are not frightened by the upheavals of the world. Let us be careful not to be deceived, and trust firmly in God's promises.
q: When you face turmoil and fear in the world, how do you keep peace in your heart? How can you grow in trusting God so that outward circumstances do not shake you?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for reminding us to trust You firmly amid the world's turmoil and the deceptions of false prophets. Give us wisdom to discern and peace in our hearts, so that in every circumstance we may fix our eyes on Your promises and keep our faith steady. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Then he said to them, “Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
There will be great earthquakes, famines, and plagues in various places. There will be terrors and great signs from heaven.
b: In this passage Jesus continues to prophesy about the last days, describing conflict between nations, earthquakes, famines, plagues, and fearful sights and great signs from heaven. These scenes are startling and show how severe the end times will be. But Jesus does not intend to make the disciples panic; He wants them to understand that these events will happen, and He urges them to keep their faith.

These prophecies remind us to hold on to our trust in God when disasters and hardships come. Although these things sound terrible, as Christians we know they are only part of what God has foretold. Our hope is not in avoiding difficulty, but in believing in God's final redemption and salvation.

Through this passage God tells us that whatever disaster or trouble we face, we should trust Him firmly. This world will go through many changes and hardships, but our God does not change. He is in control of all things; in Him we find strength and comfort, and we hold fast to our faith to the very end.
q: When disaster or hardship comes, how do you find peace and strength from God? How can you bear witness to God's faithfulness and love in difficult times?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us faith to face disaster and hardship. Help us hold fast our trust in You in every circumstance, and find peace and strength that come from You. May our lives be a witness to Your truth in this uncertain world. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: But before all these things, they will lay their hands on you and will persecute you, delivering you up to synagogues and prisons, bringing you before kings and governors for my name’s sake.
It will turn out as a testimony for you.
Settle it therefore in your hearts not to meditate beforehand how to answer,
for I will give you a mouth and wisdom which all your adversaries will not be able to withstand or to contradict.
b: In this passage Jesus foretells the persecution and challenges the disciples will face, yet He also comforts them: these hardships will become opportunities to testify to the gospel. Jesus tells them not to worry about how they will defend themselves, because at that moment He will give them wisdom and words that none of their adversaries can resist or contradict. It is an encouraging promise: whatever we face, God is with us and will give us the strength we need.

This passage reminds us that in persecution and difficulty we need not be anxious or afraid, because God will be with us and give us wisdom for every challenge. It also invites us to ask whether we are ready to witness for the Lord. Whatever the circumstances, we should rely on God's strength to express our faith.

Through this passage God reminds us that our faith should rest on God's promises, not on our own ability. Whatever difficulties or challenges we meet, God will give us the wisdom and strength we need, so that we can bear witness to Him and glorify His name before the world.
q: When your faith is challenged, do you rely on the wisdom and strength God gives you to witness for Him? How can you witness for the Lord more boldly in daily life?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for the faith and wisdom You give us when we face persecution and hardship. Help us rely on Your strength in every circumstance and witness for You without fear. May our lives reveal Your glory and be light and salt before everyone. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: You will be handed over even by parents, brothers, relatives, and friends. They will cause some of you to be put to death.
You will be hated by all men for my name’s sake.
And not a hair of your head will perish.
“By your endurance you will win your lives.
b: In this passage Jesus foretells that the disciples will face great persecution, even betrayal by their own family. Yet He also gives them great comfort: even in the hardest circumstances God keeps them, and not a hair of their head will perish. Jesus stresses the importance of endurance, for it is by endurance that they will gain their souls, a deep and steadfast faith.

This passage reminds us that, as Christians, we may meet opposition and persecution from every side, even betrayal by those closest to us. But we should not be shaken, because God's keeping is complete; He watches over every detail of our lives and gives us strength to endure to the end. We rely on God's promises and hold on to our faith until the end.

Through this passage God tells us that however dangerous our circumstances, we should keep endurance and faith, because God's protection is our eternal security. Our souls are in His care, so in every challenge we should rely on His grace and power and face the future with courage.
q: When you face challenges and difficulties in your faith, how do you keep endurance and faith? How can you rely on God's keeping to face an uncertain future?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us strength to endure when we meet difficulty and persecution. Guard our hearts, so that in every situation we can lean firmly on You to the very end. May our lives glorify Your name and bear witness to You in this world. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: “But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation is at hand.
Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains. Let those who are in the middle of her depart. Let those who are in the country not enter therein.
For these are days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.
Woe to those who are pregnant and to those who nurse infants in those days! For there will be great distress in the land, and wrath to this people.
They will fall by the edge of the sword, and will be led captive into all the nations. Jerusalem will be trampled down by the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.
b: In this passage Jesus foretells the destruction that will come upon Jerusalem because of Israel's rebellion and unbelief. He describes the coming calamity, in which those living in Jerusalem will face great danger and distress. Jesus tells the disciples that when they see these signs they should flee quickly and escape being caught up in it. It is a strong warning of the judgment about to fall on Jerusalem.

This passage reminds us that God's judgment is certain; we should pay attention to His prophecies and act according to His guidance. Jerusalem was destroyed because it rejected God's salvation, and we too should reflect on whether we are rejecting God's leading and discipline in some area of life. Let us stay spiritually alert and walk in God's will.

Through this passage God tells us that His judgment is righteous, yet also full of mercy. When we face difficulty and challenge, we should respond quickly to God's call and seek His protection and guidance. Only in God's will can we find true peace and safety.
q: When you sense God's warning or guidance, do you respond quickly and obey His will? How can you stay spiritually alert in daily life?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for reminding us to stay spiritually alert and to answer Your call quickly. Help us rely on Your guidance in trials and judgment, and find safety and keeping in You. May our lives follow Your will and be light and salt in the world. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: There will be signs in the sun, moon, and stars; and on the earth anxiety of nations, in perplexity for the roaring of the sea and the waves;
men fainting for fear, and for expectation of the things which are coming on the world: for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
Then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
But when these things begin to happen, look up and lift up your heads, because your redemption is near.”
b: In this passage Jesus describes the signs of the end, which will fill people with terror; yet for believers they are a sign that their redemption is drawing near. Jesus urges the disciples not to be afraid when they see these frightening scenes, but to stand up and lift up their heads, for the kingdom of God is near.

Jesus' words remind us that the signs of the end times are a source of fear for the world, but for believers they are the hope of our salvation. We should face these signs with a positive attitude, because they show that God's plan is being fulfilled. We should be ready at all times to welcome the Lord's return, keeping faith and hope along the way.

Through this passage God reminds us that however the world's situation changes, our eyes should be on God's promises, because He holds the future. When we see these signs, we should meet them with faith, assured that God will lead us into His kingdom. Let us keep endurance and faith as we wait for the Lord's return.
q: When you face the signs of the end times and the turmoil of the world, do you welcome the Lord's return with faith and hope? How can you keep peace in your heart along the way?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for the faith and hope You give us as we face the signs of the end. Help us, amid the changes of this world, to keep our eyes always on Your promises and to endure patiently as we wait for Your coming. May our lives be a witness to Your glory as we welcome the coming of Your kingdom. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: He told them a parable. “See the fig tree and all the trees.
When they are already budding, you see it and know by your own selves that the summer is already near.
Even so you also, when you see these things happening, know that God’s Kingdom is near.
Most certainly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all things are accomplished.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will by no means pass away.
b: In this passage Jesus uses the parable of the fig tree to teach the disciples how to discern the signs of the end. When a tree begins to sprout, people know that summer is near; likewise, when the disciples see these signs happen, they should know that the kingdom of God is near. Jesus' words also stress that His words are eternal: heaven and earth will pass away, but His words will never pass away.

This passage reminds us to stay alert, to watch what God is doing in this world, and to prepare ourselves to welcome His return. The parable of the fig tree teaches us to have spiritual sensitivity, able to discern the signs that God's kingdom is coming. We should believe firmly in Jesus' promise, because His words are forever trustworthy and are the foundation of our faith.

Through this passage God reminds us that His word is unchanging truth. We should rely on it: however this world shifts, God's promises will not change. Let us welcome His kingdom with faith and hope, and be ready for the coming of that day.
q: As you observe the changes in this world, are you sensitive to the signs of God's kingdom? How can you rely on God's eternal, unchanging word in daily life?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for the sure promises You give us through Jesus Christ. Help us, in this ever-changing world, to always believe Your words and promises, and to wait in faith for the coming of Your kingdom. May our lives be a faithful witness before You and glorify Your name. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: “So be careful, or your hearts will be loaded down with carousing, drunkenness, and cares of this life, and that day will come on you suddenly.
For it will come like a snare on all those who dwell on the surface of all the earth.
Therefore be watchful all the time, praying that you may be counted worthy to escape all these things that will happen, and to stand before the Son of Man.”
b: In this passage Jesus warns the disciples to be careful that their hearts are not weighed down by carousing, drunkenness, or the anxieties of life. He stresses the importance of watching and praying, so that when the last day comes we are not caught off guard and unable to stand before God. It is a reminder to every believer to stay spiritually sober and alert, and not be entangled by worldly things.

This passage reminds us how important it is to stay spiritually alert in a world full of temptation and pressure. Our lives are easily weighed down by daily worries and the pursuit of material things, but Jesus charges us to face all this with a watchful heart and to ask God for help continually, so that we may stand firm when He returns.

Through this passage God reminds us that the last day will come, and we should be ready to welcome it. Let us stay alert in daily life and pray constantly, so that our hearts are not bound by worldly things. Our goal should be to stand before God without fear and to enter His eternal kingdom.
q: In your busy life, do you stay alert and pray constantly? How can you make sure your heart is not entangled by worldly anxieties and temptations?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for reminding us to stay spiritually alert in this world full of temptation and pressure. Help us keep our focus on Your will at all times, and guard our hearts through prayer, so that we may stand firm when You return. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Every day Jesus was teaching in the temple, and every night he would go out and spend the night on the mountain that is called Olivet.
All the people came early in the morning to him in the temple to hear him.
b: In this passage we see that in His last days Jesus taught in the temple every day, and at night went out to the Mount of Olives to rest. This scene shows Jesus' steady commitment to teaching, and how in the midst of busy ministry He found time for quiet and rest. The people came early every morning to the temple, eager to hear Him, which shows the attraction and influence of Jesus' teaching on human hearts.

This passage reminds us that as Christians we should learn from Jesus' example: however busy we are, we should spend time in God's word and pass His teaching on to others. We also need, as Jesus did, to find time alone with God, so that we may draw strength and wisdom from Him.

Through this passage God reminds us that devotion and teaching are an important part of our life of faith. We should focus on God's word every day and let it guide our lives. However busy life is, we should set aside time to draw near to God and receive spiritual nourishment and guidance from Him.
q: In your daily life, do you regularly spend time in God's word and draw near to Him? How can you keep the habit of devotion in a busy schedule?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for setting us an example through Jesus Christ, teaching us to focus on Your word in every circumstance. Help us find time to draw near to You in our busy lives, and to put Your teaching into practice. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Now the feast of unleavened bread, which is called the Passover, was approaching.
The chief priests and the scribes sought how they might put him to death, for they feared the people.
Satan entered into Judas, who was also called Iscariot, who was counted with the twelve.
He went away, and talked with the chief priests and captains about how he might deliver him to them.
They were glad, and agreed to give him money.
He consented, and sought an opportunity to deliver him to them in the absence of the multitude.
b: This passage describes the plot that led to Jesus' betrayal. The chief priests and scribes, afraid of Jesus' influence, looked for a way to put Him to death. Their fear and envy led them to scheme against Him. Judas, under Satan's influence, decided to betray Jesus and made a deal with the religious leaders to hand Him over for silver. These events mark the opening of Jesus' passion and reveal the corruption of the human heart and the depth of sin.

This passage reminds us how sin can control and destroy a soul. Judas was one of Jesus' disciples, but by giving himself over to greed and betrayal he became the instrument of Jesus' betrayal. We must be watchful over the motives and choices of our own hearts, so that worldly gain does not lead us off the right path. Let us stay alert at all times, lest like Judas we are drawn by temptation onto a wrong road.

Through this passage God tells us that the power of sin is strong, but we can choose not to be controlled by it. Let us act carefully and not let our hearts be occupied by evil thoughts. Only by relying on God's grace and guidance can we resist temptation and keep a pure heart.
q: Have you faced temptation in your life? How do you choose to stay on the right path and not turn aside?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for warning us of the danger of sin and the power of temptation. Guard our hearts, so that we may stay on the right path and not be led by temptation. May we walk in Your grace and not fall, like Judas, into the abyss of betrayal. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: The day of unleavened bread came, on which the Passover must be sacrificed.
Jesus sent Peter and John, saying, “Go and prepare the Passover for us, that we may eat.”
They said to him, “Where do you want us to prepare?”
He said to them, “Behold, when you have entered into the city, a man carrying a pitcher of water will meet you. Follow him into the house which he enters.
Tell the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says to you, “Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?” ’
He will show you a large, furnished upper room. Make preparations there.”
They went, found things as Jesus had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
b: This passage records how Jesus told the disciples to prepare for the Passover. His instructions were very detailed, even describing the person they would meet, which shows His full command of every circumstance. The disciples obeyed, found the furnished upper room, and prepared the Passover meal there. The scene shows how fully Jesus had prepared for the suffering ahead, and also stresses the importance of obeying His will.

This passage reminds us that as Christians we should listen to God's guidance at all times, in great matters and small. God has a complete plan for our lives, and He will lead us along the path He has prepared. Our responsibility is to obey and trust His leading; however uncertain or hard the road ahead may look, God's plan is always for our good.

Through this passage God tells us that His guidance is precise and full of wisdom. We need to learn to rely on His leading in life, not acting on our own understanding but trusting His plan and arrangement. As we obey God, we will experience His faithfulness and grace.
q: When you face decisions and challenges in life, do you trust and depend on God's guidance? How can you learn to listen to His leading in every detail?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for guiding us in every detail of our lives. Help us rely on Your leading at all times and obey Your will. May we see Your faithfulness and grace in every decision of our lives. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: When the hour had come, he sat down with the twelve apostles.
He said to them, “I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer,
for I tell you, I will no longer by any means eat of it until it is fulfilled in God’s Kingdom.”
He received a cup, and when he had given thanks, he said, “Take this, and share it among yourselves,
for I tell you, I will not drink at all again from the fruit of the vine, until God’s Kingdom comes.”
He took bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke, and gave it to them, saying, “This is my body which is given for you. Do this in memory of me.”
Likewise, he took the cup after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you.
b: This passage records Jesus' last supper with His disciples, the moment the Lord's Supper was instituted. At this meal Jesus expressed deeply His love for the disciples and His intention to suffer and die for the sins of all people. He took the bread and the cup, symbolizing His body and blood, and told the disciples to keep this remembrance until the kingdom of God fully comes. This act deeply reveals Jesus' plan of redemption and His boundless sacrifice and love for us.

This passage reminds us that the Lord's Supper is an important part of a Christian's life of faith; it is not merely a ritual but a remembrance of Jesus Christ's sacrifice. Each time we receive it we should do so with thankfulness, remember that Jesus gave His life for us, and reflect on our relationship with Him. Jesus established the new covenant with His body and blood, and on that foundation we should live lives worthy of Him.

Through this passage God tells us that Jesus' love and sacrifice are boundless; we should remember Him often and put His teaching into practice in daily life. The Lord's Supper reminds us that Jesus has paid the highest price for us, and His love is our strength and guide every day.
q: When you receive the Lord's Supper, do you truly realize its meaning? How can you remember and practice Jesus' teaching in daily life?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving Jesus Christ, who gave His life for us and established the new covenant. Help us, each time we receive the Lord's Supper, to remember His sacrifice with thankful hearts and to live lives worthy of Him. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: But behold, the hand of him who betrays me is with me on the table.
The Son of Man indeed goes, as it has been determined, but woe to that man through whom he is betrayed!”
They began to question among themselves, which of them it was who would do this thing.
b: In this passage, at the last supper, Jesus makes clear that the one who will betray Him is sitting at the table with Him. This shows that Jesus knew fully what was about to happen; He knew Judas would betray Him, yet it did not change His determination to complete the plan of redemption. His words strongly condemn the betrayer's deed and warn that it will bring him endless woe.

This passage reminds us that Jesus' plan of redemption was determined by God, and no one's betrayal or sin can stop its fulfillment. Yet this does not mean that those who choose to betray and sin are free from responsibility. Judas' choice led to his final ruin, warning us to choose our actions and path carefully and not to walk the road of betraying God.

Through this passage God tells us that His plan cannot be stopped, but each of us is responsible to choose the path of integrity. Let us constantly reflect on our actions and motives, making sure we walk in a way pleasing to God, and not fall, like Judas, into the abyss of betrayal.
q: When you face a choice, do you consider whether your actions agree with God's will? How can you keep your integrity in daily life and avoid straying from God's path?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for reminding us, through the words of Jesus Christ, to choose the path of integrity. Help us make choices in life that please You, and avoid the road of betrayal and sin. May our lives glorify Your name. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: A dispute also arose among them, which of them was considered to be greatest.
He said to them, “The kings of the nations lord it over them, and those who have authority over them are called ‘benefactors.’
But not so with you. But one who is the greater among you, let him become as the younger, and one who is governing, as one who serves.
For who is greater, one who sits at the table, or one who serves? Isn’t it he who sits at the table? But I am among you as one who serves.
b: This passage records the disciples' argument at the last supper about who was the greatest. Jesus uses it to teach them that true greatness is not in power or position but in serving others. Jesus Himself, their Lord, came among them as one who serves; His example clearly shows that greatness lies in humility and service, not in pursuing personal glory and power.

This passage reminds us that as Jesus' disciples we should set aside the world's values, learn from Christ's example, and serve others with a humble heart. True greatness lies in how we love and serve others, not in how much power or position we hold. When we follow Christ's example, our lives reflect God's love and grace.

Through this passage God tells us that serving others is the mark of greatness in God's kingdom. We should lay down our pride and humble ourselves, and like Jesus show God's love and grace by serving others. Our lives should not pursue worldly glory but the greatness that is real in God's eyes.
q: In your life, how do you serve others with humility? Are you willing to lay down your pride and become a servant to others, as Jesus did?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us through Jesus Christ that true greatness lies in serving others. Give us humble hearts, that like Jesus we may be willing to lay ourselves down and serve others. May our lives show Your love and grace and glorify Your name. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: But you are those who have continued with me in my trials.
I confer on you a kingdom, even as my Father conferred on me,
that you may eat and drink at my table in my Kingdom. You will sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”
b: In this passage Jesus thanks the disciples for their faithfulness and promises them an important place in God's kingdom. Although the disciples were still full of weakness and failure during Jesus' trials, Jesus firmly gave them the promise of the kingdom. He says that in the coming kingdom they will eat and drink at His table and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

This passage reminds us that although we will face trials and challenges on the path of faith, Jesus promises that if we hold fast to our faith we will in the end share in glory in God's kingdom. Jesus' promise encourages us to follow Him faithfully even in hardship, because He has prepared eternal glory and reward for us.

Through this passage God tells us that He greatly rewards our faith and faithfulness. When we face hardship and trial we should hold fast to our faith, because we know that God has prepared for us a glory and joy beyond this present age. Our faithfulness and faith will be rewarded in the coming kingdom, and in this life they become a source of our strength.
q: When you face trials of faith, how do you keep your faith firm? Do you look forward to God's promises in the coming kingdom and let them motivate you?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for promising us glory and reward in Your kingdom. Help us hold fast to our faith in trials and follow You faithfully. May our lives glorify Your name, and may we share in Your rich promises in the coming kingdom. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: The Lord said, “Simon, Simon, behold, Satan asked to have all of you, that he might sift you as wheat,
but I prayed for you, that your faith wouldn’t fail. You, when once you have turned again, establish your brothers.”
He said to him, “Lord, I am ready to go with you both to prison and to death!”
He said, “I tell you, Peter, the rooster will by no means crow today until you deny that you know me three times.”
b: In this passage Jesus foretells that Peter will deny Him three times during His passion, revealing the weakness of human nature. Although Peter confidently said he was ready to go with the Lord to prison and to death, Jesus knew that Peter's faith would waver. Even so, Jesus did not give up on Peter; He prayed for him that his faith would not fail completely, and encouraged him to strengthen the other disciples once he had turned back.

This passage reminds us that, as Christians, each of us may experience weakness and failure when our faith is tested. Yet Jesus not only understands our weakness, He also intercedes for us, helping us stand up again after we fall, and then use that experience to encourage others. We should learn from Peter's experience: although we may sometimes fall, if we turn back we can still be used by the Lord.

Through this passage God tells us that His love and grace toward us are endless; even when we are weak in faith, He is still willing to support us. Let us take this as motivation, not only to rely on the Lord in weakness, but after setbacks to become strength and support for others.
q: When you experience setbacks in your faith, how do you rely on the Lord's strength to stand up again? Are you willing to use your own experience to help and encourage others?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for Your love and patience toward us. When we are weak in faith, help us rely on Your strength to stand up again. After our setbacks, may we become encouragement and support to others, and grow in Your grace. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: He said to them, “When I sent you out without purse, wallet, and sandals, did you lack anything?” They said, “Nothing.”
Then he said to them, “But now, whoever has a purse, let him take it, and likewise a wallet. Whoever has none, let him sell his cloak, and buy a sword.
For I tell you that this which is written must still be fulfilled in me: ‘He was counted with transgressors.’ For that which concerns me has an end.”
They said, “Lord, behold, here are two swords.” He said to them, “That is enough.”
b: This passage records Jesus' new instructions to the disciples after the last supper. He reminds them that in the past, when they had no purse, bag, or sandals, they lacked nothing. But now things are different: Jesus is about to be arrested and put to death, and the disciples need to prepare for the hardship ahead, even to the point of having a sword to protect themselves. Jesus quotes the Scripture that He will be counted among the lawless, marking the suffering and sacrifice He is about to go through.

This passage reminds us that the path of faith is not always smooth, and sometimes we need to prepare for challenge and persecution. Jesus told the disciples to take swords not to encourage violence, but to help them understand the hard situation ahead. We too should prepare ourselves on our journey of faith, both spiritually and in practical life, for possible trials and challenges.

Through this passage God tells us that faith needs steadfastness and preparation. We should not only rely on God's provision, but also prepare wisely for the challenges ahead. When we face persecution or hardship, we need to stand firm in faith, knowing that God has prepared a way out and help for us.
q: When you face challenges in life or faith, how do you prepare for them? Do you rely on God's strength to face the difficulties ahead?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us to be prepared in faith for the challenges ahead. Give us wisdom and courage, so that we may walk steadfastly in Your way and, whatever difficulty we face, rely on Your strength. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: He came out and went, as his custom was, to the Mount of Olives. His disciples also followed him.
When he was at the place, he said to them, “Pray that you don’t enter into temptation.”
He was withdrawn from them about a stone’s throw, and he knelt down and prayed,
saying, “Father, if you are willing, remove this cup from me. Nevertheless, not my will, but yours, be done.”
An angel from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him.
Being in agony he prayed more earnestly. His sweat became like great drops of blood falling down on the ground.
When he rose up from his prayer, he came to the disciples, and found them sleeping because of grief,
and said to them, “Why do you sleep? Rise and pray that you may not enter into temptation.”
b: This passage records Jesus' prayer on the Mount of Olives, one of His most painful moments before the cross. Jesus knew the suffering He was about to bear, and in prayer He asked the Father that, if possible, this cup be taken from Him. Yet in the end He chose to submit to God's will, showing His complete humility and obedience. The disciples fell asleep from sorrow, and Jesus again urged them to watch and pray so that they would not fall into temptation.

This passage reminds us that in the hardships and temptations of life, prayer is our most powerful weapon. By His own example Jesus teaches us that even in the hardest moments we should submit to God's will, rather than rely on our own strength or wisdom. We should stay alert at all times and seek God's strength and guidance in prayer, so that we do not fall into temptation.

Through this passage God tells us that submitting to His will takes great faith and courage. We should seek His guidance in prayer and believe that His plan is best. When we face hardship, we need, like Jesus, to be willing to yield to God's arrangement and receive strength in prayer.
q: When you face difficulty or temptation, how do you seek God's strength and guidance through prayer? Are you willing, like Jesus, to submit fully to God's will?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us, through Jesus' prayer, how to rely on You in hardship. Help us stay alert, seek Your will in prayer, and have faith to submit to Your arrangement. May we, like Jesus, make prayer our source of strength when we face life's challenges. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: While he was still speaking, behold, a multitude, and he who was called Judas, one of the twelve, was leading them. He came near to Jesus to kiss him.
But Jesus said to him, “Judas, do you betray the Son of Man with a kiss?”
When those who were around him saw what was about to happen, they said to him, “Lord, shall we strike with the sword?”
A certain one of them struck the servant of the high priest, and cut off his right ear.
But Jesus answered, “Let me at least do this”—and he touched his ear, and healed him.
Jesus said to the chief priests, captains of the temple, and elders, who had come against him, “Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs?
When I was with you in the temple daily, you didn’t stretch out your hands against me. But this is your hour, and the power of darkness.”
b: This passage records Jesus' arrest in the Garden of Gethsemane. Judas used a kiss as the signal to betray Jesus, revealing human weakness and the treachery of sin. Facing the disciples' rashness and the enemies' attack, Jesus remained calm, and even at the moment of His arrest He healed the ear of the high priest's servant, showing His boundless compassion and kindness. He told those who came to seize Him that they were acting under the power of darkness; this was the hour of the forces of evil.

This passage reminds us that even in betrayal and danger, Jesus still showed His divine nature and love. When we face hardship and challenge in life, we should follow His example, staying calm and loving rather than being controlled by emotion and fear. Though the powers of darkness may at times seem to hold the situation, we should believe firmly that God's final victory is certain.

Through this passage God tells us that whatever trouble or betrayal we face, His love and mercy never change. Let us learn from Jesus to keep showing love to others in hard times, and trust God's final plan. Remember that even in the dark hour, God's light will in the end overcome everything.
q: When you face betrayal or hardship, how can you, like Jesus, stay calm and show love? Do you believe in God's final victory, and stay firm in faith in difficulty?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us, through Jesus' example, to show love and calm even in hardship. Give us courage and wisdom, so that when we face betrayal and challenge we may trust Your plan and answer everything with Your love. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: They seized him, and led him away, and brought him into the high priest’s house. But Peter followed from a distance.
When they had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard, and had sat down together, Peter sat among them.
A certain servant girl saw him as he sat in the light, and looking intently at him, said, “This man also was with him.”
He denied Jesus, saying, “Woman, I don’t know him.”
After a little while someone else saw him, and said, “You also are one of them!” But Peter answered, “Man, I am not!”
After about one hour passed, another confidently affirmed, saying, “Truly this man also was with him, for he is a Galilean!”
But Peter said, “Man, I don’t know what you are talking about!” Immediately, while he was still speaking, a rooster crowed.
The Lord turned and looked at Peter. Then Peter remembered the Lord’s word, how he said to him, “Before the rooster crows you will deny me three times.”
He went out, and wept bitterly.
b: 這段經文描述了彼得三次不認主的場景，這是彼得生命中最痛苦的時刻之一。儘管彼得在之前信誓旦旦地表示願意為主捨命，但在面對實際的壓力和危險時，他卻屢次否認認識耶穌。當雞叫聲響起時，彼得猛然醒悟，回想起耶穌的預言，內心深感懊悔。這一時刻，耶穌的目光與彼得相遇，彼得的心被深深觸動，他出來痛哭，這顯示了他對自己軟弱的深刻認識和悔改的心。

and if I ask, you will in no way answer me or let me go.
From now on, the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God.”
They all said, “Are you then the Son of God?” He said to them, “You say it, because I am.”

v: Pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers, and the people,

and said to them, “You brought this man to me as one that perverts the people, and behold, having examined him before you, I found no basis for a charge against this man concerning those things of which you accuse him.
Neither has Herod, for I sent you to him, and see, nothing worthy of death has been done by him.
I will therefore chastise him and release him.”
Now he had to release one prisoner to them at the feast.
But they all cried out together, saying, “Away with this man! Release to us Barabbas!”—
one who was thrown into prison for a certain revolt in the city, and for murder.
Then Pilate spoke to them again, wanting to release Jesus,
but they shouted, saying, “Crucify! Crucify him!”

But they were urgent with loud voices, asking that he might be crucified. Their voices and the voices of the chief priests prevailed.
Pilate decreed that what they asked for should be done.
He released him who had been thrown into prison for insurrection and murder, for whom they asked, but he delivered Jesus up to their will.
b: 這段經文記載了彼拉多在面對群眾壓力時，最終妥協，將無罪的耶穌交給他們釘十字架的經過。彼拉多在審問後，發現耶穌沒有犯下任何罪行，甚至連希律也無法定祂的罪。然而，當他試圖釋放耶穌時，卻面臨群眾的強烈抗議，他們寧願釋放一個罪犯巴拉巴，也不願放過耶穌。面對這種壓力，彼拉多最終屈服於群眾的要求，將耶穌交給他們。

But as many as received him, to them he gave the right to become God’s children, to those who believe in his name:
who were born not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.
b: 這段經文指出神差遣施洗約翰，目的不是成為光，而是引導人來到光的面前。人容易把焦點放在人身上，容易把人高舉起來，但約翰清楚自己的身份——他不是光，他只是指向光的人。他的角色提醒我們，真正值得注目、值得跟隨的是耶穌，而不是任何人。當焦點放在耶穌身上，人心才能對齊，方向才能正確。
經文接著說，耶穌是真光，祂照亮每一個來到世界上的人。光一照，就使人看見生命的本相、內心的實況，也帶來得救的道路。然而，雖然世界是藉祂造的，人卻不認識祂；祂到自己的地方來，祂的百姓反不接待祂。這是人心的悲哀——神親自來找人，但人卻拒絕光，拒絕真理，拒絕生命。
然而，故事沒有停在拒絕，而是轉向極大的恩典。十二節說：「凡接待他的，就是信他名的人，他就賜他們權柄，作神的兒女。」這不是靠血統、不是靠努力、更不是靠人的決心，而是神親自重生我們，使我們成為祂的兒女。
成為神兒女意味著生命的身份完全改變。我們不再屬於世界，不再靠自己，不再被罪與黑暗轄制，而是有一個屬天的身份，有光的生命，有神兒女的權柄。這是一個全新的開始，是從神生的生命，是讓耶穌在我們裡面活的生命。
q: 你是否真的讓耶穌成為你生命的光？在日常生活中，你如何活出神兒女的身份？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝祢差遣真光來到世上，使我們在黑暗中看見盼望。求祢賜給我們柔軟的心，不拒絕光，不拒絕真理，願意接待耶穌，使我們真正活出神兒女的身份。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。

v: The Word became flesh, and lived among us. We saw his glory, such glory as of the one and only Son of the Father, full of grace and truth.
John testified about him. He cried out, saying, “This was he of whom I said, ‘He who comes after me has surpassed me, for he was before me.’ ”
From his fullness we all received grace upon grace.
For the law was given through Moses. Grace and truth were realized through Jesus Christ.
No one has seen God at any time. The one and only Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, has declared him.
b: 「道成了肉身」揭開了神救恩計畫最深的奧祕。永恆的道本來與父同在、就是神，如今卻披上人的身體，走進人的世界。祂選擇與我們同住，使人可以在祂的生活、祂的表情、祂的話語、祂的腳蹤中，看見天父的榮光。祂不是遠方的神，而是近在身旁、可以觸碰、可以相遇的主。
經文說，我們從祂豐滿的恩典裡「都領受了，而且恩上加恩」。祂不是只給一次恩典，而是不斷加添，使我們在每一個需要中，都得著新的力量。律法指出人的不足，但耶穌帶來的恩典使我們能站起來；律法讓人知道該做什麼，但耶穌給出活出真理的能力。祂的恩典不是補強舊生命，而是賜下新的生命，使我們靠祂而活，而不是靠自己。
最後，約翰告訴我們，從來沒有人看見神，只有在父懷裡的獨生子將祂表明出來。耶穌不是僅僅講述關於神的知識，而是把神的心完全展現在人面前。想知道神如何看待我們，看耶穌如何接納軟弱的人；想知道神的聖潔，看耶穌如何面對罪；想知道神的愛，看耶穌如何捨己、如何服事。耶穌向我們顯明父的心，使我們不再靠猜測，而是靠認識祂來認識神。
q: 你現在最需要領受的是哪一種恩典？主今天要如何在你的生命中，加添祂的恩上加恩？
pr: 親愛的天父，謝謝祢讓耶穌成為道成肉身的主，使我們能在祂身上看見祢的榮光。求祢的恩典不斷加添，使我們不依靠自己，而是倚靠祢的能力活每一天。願我們藉著認識耶穌，更深認識祢的心。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。

v: This is John’s testimony, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, “Who are you?”
He declared, and didn’t deny, but he declared, “I am not the Christ.”
They asked him, “What then? Are you Elijah?” He said, “I am not.” “Are you the prophet?” He answered, “No.”
They said therefore to him, “Who are you? Give us an answer to take back to those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?”
He said, “I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Make straight the way of the Lord,’ as Isaiah the prophet said.”
b: 這段經文帶我們看見施洗約翰對自己角色的清楚認識。他在神面前謙卑，也在人面前誠實。當宗教領袖問他：「你是誰？」約翰立刻表明：「我不是基督。」他沒有試圖高舉自己，也沒有假借神的名讓自己得到地位或掌聲。他知道自己的位置，也知道自己只是預備道路的人，而不是道路本身。
宗教領袖接著追問他是否是以利亞或那位預言中的大先知，約翰也一一否認。他不願攬取不屬於自己的榮耀，也不願接受人錯誤的期待。他拒絕把人帶到自己面前，而是要帶到神面前。這種心是屬於新人的心——不是想抓住權力，而是願意放下；不是為了自己，而是為了主。
當他們再度追問：「你到底是誰？」約翰回答：「我就是那在曠野有人聲喊著說：修直主的道路。」他引用以賽亞書的預言，指出自己唯一的使命就是預備人的心，讓主的道路被修直。約翰知道，他不是光，他只是指向光的聲音；他不是救主，他只是引導人到救主那裡的器皿。
這提醒我們：在服事中，我們真正的價值不在於位置高低，而在於是否把焦點放在主身上。神能使用一顆謙卑的心，也能將祂的榮光透過我們彰顯出來，只要我們願意在祂面前站對位置，不搶祂的榮耀，不代替祂作王。
q: 在你目前的服事與生活中，有哪些領域需要再次調整心態，把位置讓給主，讓祂的道路在你裡面被修直？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝祢透過約翰的生命教導我們謙卑、順服與忠心。求祢讓我們認識自己的位置，不高舉自己，不抓住不屬於自己的位置，而是願意修直祢的道路，使人能透過我們更清楚看見耶穌。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。

v: The ones who had been sent were from the Pharisees.
They asked him, “Why then do you baptize, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the prophet?”
John answered them, “I baptize in water, but among you stands one whom you don’t know.
He is the one who comes after me, who is preferred before me, whose sandal strap I’m not worthy to loosen.”
These things were done in Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
b: 那些人是法利赛人差来的；他们就问他说：“你既不是基督，不是以利亚，也不是那先知，为什么施洗呢？”约翰回答说：“我是用水施洗，但有一位站在你们中间，是你们不认识的，就是那在我以后来的，我给他解鞋带也不配。”这是在约旦河外伯大尼，约翰施洗的地方作的见证。
法利賽人看見約翰在施洗，就質疑他：「你不是基督、不是以利亞，也不是那先知，那你憑什麼施洗？」這是典型的宗教心態——關注權柄從哪裡來、資格是否足夠、位置是否正確。他們習慣按人的標準衡量屬靈事工，卻看不見神正在做的新事，看不見神已經在他們中間的作為。
約翰的回答卻扎根在深深的謙卑中。他說：「我用水施洗，但有一位站在你們中間，是你們不認識的。」他不是為自己辯護，而是再次把焦點指向那位真正重要的主。他施洗只是預備人的心，但真正能改變生命的，是那位他們尚未認識、卻已經在場的耶穌。
接著約翰說：「我連給祂解鞋帶也不配。」在當時，解鞋帶是最低微僕人的工作，而約翰卻認為自己連這樣服事耶穌都不配。這不是自卑，而是一種看見神真實榮美後自然湧出的謙卑。當人越認識基督，越明白祂的偉大；當人越靠近光，越看見自己的有限。這正是被聖靈引導的生命——不抓權力、不自我高舉，而是全心讓主的榮光彰顯。
最後，經文記錄了場景：這些事發生在約旦河外伯大尼。這裡不是焦點，因為焦點不是地點，而是那位站在人中間、卻常被忽略的耶穌。神的工作常常如此——祂就在我們之中，但若我們的眼目在自己、在制度、在環境，就容易錯過神正在做的事。
q: 生活中，哪些地方容易讓你「看見人卻看不見耶穌」？今天，你願意調整眼目，認出那位已經在你中間的主嗎？
pr: 親愛的天父，求祢幫助我們，不落入宗教的眼光，不靠自己的判斷衡量祢的工作，而是能謙卑、順服、敏銳地看見耶穌正在我們中間。讓我們像約翰一樣，把焦點放在祢的兒子身上，讓祢的榮光而不是我們的自己被看見。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。

v: The next day, he saw Jesus coming to him, and said, “Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!
This is he of whom I said, ‘After me comes a man who is preferred before me, for he was before me.’
I didn’t know him, but for this reason I came baptizing in water: that he would be revealed to Israel.”
John testified, saying, “I have seen the Spirit descending like a dove out of heaven, and it remained on him.
I didn’t recognize him, but he who sent me to baptize in water said to me, ‘On whomever you will see the Spirit descending and remaining on him is he who baptizes in the Holy Spirit.’
I have seen, and have testified that this is the Son of God.”
b: 次日，约翰看见耶稣来到他那里，就说：“看哪，　神的羔羊，除去世人罪孽的！这就是我曾说：‘有一位在我以后来、反成了在我以前的，因他本来在我以前。’；我先前不认识他，如今我来用水施洗，为要叫他显明给以色列人。”；约翰又作见证说：“我曾看见圣灵，仿佛鸽子从天降下，住在他的身上。我先前不认识他，只是那差我来用水施洗的、对我说：‘你看见圣灵降下来，住在谁的身上，谁就是用圣灵施洗的。’；我看见了，就证明这是　神的儿子。”
在眾人尋求悔改、尋求方向、尋求救恩的時刻，約翰指著耶穌說：「看哪，神的羔羊，除去世人罪孽的！」不是看他，不是看環境，不是看宗教制度，而是「看耶穌」。祂是神所預備的救贖，是所有獻祭制度的成全，是唯一能真正除去罪、拆掉隔絕、恢復與父連結的那一位。人最大的問題是罪，而最大的答案只有基督。
約翰接著說：「祂本來在我以前。」雖然耶穌肉身的年齡比約翰小，卻「原本在先」。這說明耶穌不是普通人，也不是從出生才開始存在，而是從永恆中與父同在的那位。祂來，不是開始，而是顯明；不是被造，而是道成肉身。
約翰也兩次提到：「我先前不認識祂。」這不是說他不知道耶穌這個人，而是指他不知道耶穌的真實身份。直到聖靈親自顯明，讓他看見從天降下、停留在祂身上的聖靈，這才確定祂是那位用聖靈施洗的主。人靠自己的分析永遠無法認出基督，但聖靈的光一照，真理就清晰；聖靈一引導，人心就能看見耶穌的真實。
最終，約翰說：「我看見了，就證明這是神的兒子。」他不是靠感覺、不是靠猜測，而是靠從神來的啟示做見證。真正的信仰，就是讓聖靈帶我們看見耶穌，並把榮耀單單歸給祂。
q: 你今天的眼目在看什麼？是在看環境、看自己、還是看耶穌這位「除去罪孽的羔羊」？你願意重新把焦點調回祂身上嗎？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝祢讓我們看見耶穌是神的羔羊，是我們唯一的拯救。求祢讓聖靈天天引導我們，使我們不靠自己判斷，而是看見祂的真實、祂的榮耀、祂的救恩。願我們的眼目常常定睛在祢的兒子身上。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。

v: Again, the next day, John was standing with two of his disciples,
and he looked at Jesus as he walked, and said, “Behold, the Lamb of God!”
The two disciples heard him speak, and they followed Jesus.
Jesus turned and saw them following, and said to them, “What are you looking for?” They said to him, “Rabbi” (which is to say, being interpreted, Teacher), “where are you staying?”
He said to them, “Come, and see.” They came and saw where he was staying, and they stayed with him that day. It was about the tenth hour.
b: 再次日，约翰同两个门徒站在那里。他见耶稣行走，就说：“看哪，这是　神的羔羊！”；两个门徒听见他的话，就跟从了耶稣。耶稣转过身来，看见他们跟着，就问他们说：“你们要什么？”；他们说：“拉比，在哪里住？”（拉比翻出来就是夫子。）耶稣说：“你们来看。”他们就去看他在哪里住，这一天便与他同住；那时约有申正了。
施洗約翰第三次指出耶穌，說：「看哪，神的羔羊！」他沒有吸引人到自己身邊，而是把人帶往基督。真正屬神的人不是讓別人依賴自己，而是使人越來越靠近主、認識主、跟隨主。當焦點放在耶穌身上，人的生命自然會被吸引走向光。
兩個門徒聽見這句話後，立刻離開約翰，跟從耶穌。這不是背叛，而是成熟的開始。任何屬靈的教導、牧養或帶領，最終的目的都不是使人依附於人，而是帶人來到耶穌面前，使人親自與主連結、親自經歷祂。人的影響只是開端，與主同行才是生命真正的道路。
耶穌轉身問他們：「你們要什麼？」這是主今天也問我們的問題。祂不是問他們想得到什麼，而是問他們的心──你們在尋找什麼？你們真正渴慕的是誰？兩位門徒的回答不是要祝福、不是要神蹟，而是：「你在哪裡住？」也就是：「我們想更深、更近地認識祢。我們想和祢在一起。」這是一顆真門徒的心──渴望主本身，而不是主所賜的東西。
耶穌的回應是：「你們來看。」祂沒有講道理，沒有多作解釋，而是邀請他們「親自來、親自看、親自經歷」。信仰不是知識，而是關係；不是遠遠觀望，而是跟祂住在一起。兩個門徒那一天與主同住，生命的方向從此徹底改變。
q: 若今天耶穌問你：「你要什麼？」你的心會如何回答？你渴望祂的祝福，還是渴望祂自己？
pr: 親愛的天父，謝謝祢吸引我們來到耶穌面前。求祢使我們的心不只想要祢的恩典，更渴慕祢自己。願我們回應祢的呼召，天天來看、來親近、來與祢同住，使我們的生命因為與祢同行而更新。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。

v: One of the two who heard John and followed him was Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother.
He first found his own brother, Simon, and said to him, “We have found the Messiah!” (which is, being interpreted, Christ).
He brought him to Jesus. Jesus looked at him, and said, “You are Simon the son of Jonah. You shall be called Cephas” (which is by interpretation, Peter).
b: 听见约翰的话跟从耶稣的那两个人，一个是西门·彼得的兄弟安得烈。他先找着自己的哥哥西门，对他说：“我们遇见弥赛亚了。”（弥赛亚翻出来就是基督。）于是领他去见耶稣。耶稣看着他，说：“你是约翰的儿子西门，你要称为矶法。”（矶法翻出来就是彼得。）
在這段經文中，我們看見福音最美的流動方式：一個人遇見耶穌，就把最親近的人帶到耶穌面前。安得烈並不是十二使徒中最知名的，也不是領袖人物，但他做了一件至關重要的事──把彼得帶到主的面前，而彼得將來成為教會的柱石，影響無數世代。
這提醒我們：神常常使用那些默默無名、沒有舞台、沒有聚光燈的人，來成就祂國度最重要的工作。神不是看外貌、背景或能力，而是看一顆願意的心。願意尋求祂的，就會遇見祂；願意分享祂的，就會成為祝福。每一次把人帶到耶穌面前，雖然看似平凡，卻可能改變一個人的永恆，也改變無數人的命運。
當彼得來到耶穌面前，主第一句話不是責備、不是命令，而是從眼中看出他的將來，並為他取了新名字：「你要稱為磯法。」就是「磐石」的意思。耶穌不是看彼得現在的樣子，而是看他在主手中將會成為的樣子。祂看见的是命定，是呼召，是未來的榮耀，而不是缺點與軟弱。
彼得的本性衝動、多變、容易跌倒，但耶穌看見他被神塑造後的樣貌──堅定、剛強、可靠。主對待我們也是如此：祂不是被我們的過去定義，而是用祂的生命重塑我們，使我們成為祂眼中所看見的那個新人。
q: 你生命中是否有「彼得」這樣的人，神正在等你把他帶到耶穌面前？今天，你願意成為福音流動的「安得烈」嗎？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝祢使我們能遇見耶穌，也求祢給我們一顆願意的心，把人帶到祢面前。求祢讓我們像安得烈一樣，看中每一個靈魂。也求祢開我們的眼，使我們看見祢對我們生命的呼召與命定，願我們在祢手中成為新的人。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
